title: Which of these five pairs of numbers are co-prime?
description: The factors of the numbers in each pair are compared, and the pairs with only one in common are picked out. Keeko doubts that eighty one and eighteen are co-prime, because one is odd and one is even.
teaching_notes: One idea: a pair is co-prime only when its factor lists share just one, so a pair with an odd and an even number can still share a factor. Watch for students who decide by how the two numbers look.

source: Which of the following pairs of numbers are co-prime? a. 18
video_script.why: The child lists the factors that matter in each pair and marks a pair co-prime only when no factor other than one is shared.
video_script.substitution: For each pair, look for a factor other than one that divides both numbers.
video_script.anchor: Five pairs of number cards in a column, each waiting for a co-prime or not co-prime tag
video_script.wrong_answer: eighty one and eighteen are co-prime
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks eighty one and eighteen are co-prime because one is odd and one is even, but three divides both numbers.
video_script.payoff_line: The first, second and fourth pairs are co-prime.

final_answer.value: a, b and d are co-prime
final_answer.spoken: the first, second and fourth pairs

maths_rules: co-prime: no common factor other than 1
17 (a prime) and 69 = 3 × 23: 17 does not divide 69, so only 1 is shared
81 and 18: 3 divides both, since 81 = 3 × 27 and 18 = 3 × 6; 9 divides both too
video_script.design: Five pairs of cards sit in a column; each gets a tag that turns teal for co-prime and amber when a shared factor is found.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about co-prime pairs.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Five pairs are given. The first two are eighteen and thirty five, and fifteen and thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Then come thirty and four hundred and fifteen, and seventeen and sixty nine.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last is eighty one and eighteen. Which pairs are co-prime?

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>Two numbers are co-prime when they have no common factor other than one.
<bookmark mark='look'/>For each pair, we look for one factor, other than one, that divides both numbers.

narration: <bookmark mark='eighteen'/>Step one, take the first and second pairs. Eighteen has one, two, three, six, nine and eighteen.
<bookmark mark='thirtyfive'/>Thirty five has one, five, seven and thirty five. Only the factor one is shared.

<bookmark mark='fifteenb'/>Fifteen does not have thirty seven as a factor. Only the factor one is shared by these two numbers as well.

beats.on_screen: 30 = 5 × 6 and 415 = 5 × 83: 5 divides both | 81 = 3 × 27 and 18 = 3 × 6: 3 divides both

<bookmark mark='eighty'/>Eighty one is three times twenty seven, and eighteen is three times six.
<bookmark mark='threecommon'/>The number three is a common factor of both.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eighty one and eighteen are co-prime, because one is odd and one is even.
<bookmark mark='reason'/>But three divides eighty one, and three divides eighteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Odd or even does not decide it. A shared factor does.
